skill.name: css
skill.description: Implements or debugs CSS layout, responsive sizing, cascade, selectors, and styling performance. Use for concrete stylesheet work; visual-system design and UX reviews belong to web-design-guidelines.
skill.summary: Implement and debug modern CSS layouts, responsive components, cascade rules, themes, and rendering performance.
skill.author: shreyam1008

security_audit.summary: Thirty-five findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, CSS syntax, or browser rendering advice. One finding is confirmed: the optional reference command uses npx with an unpinned latest package, allowing externally supplied code to execute. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The reference command at SKILL.md:74 can execute an unpinned npm package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a documentation link; otherwise verify package provenance, pin a reviewed version, and require explicit user approval before execution.

content.value_statement: CSS layout bugs and conflicting rules make responsive interfaces difficult to maintain. This skill guides stylesheet changes using modern layout, cascade, theming, and performance techniques.
actual_capabilities: Guide Flexbox and Grid choices, spacing, logical properties, and overflow fixes.
Apply container queries, intrinsic sizing, viewport units, aspect ratios, and subgrid patterns.
Explain cascade layers, selector specificity, native nesting, and scoped styles.
Recommend state selectors, focus styling, and browser-support fallbacks.
Organize custom properties, design tokens, and theme overrides.
Review animation properties, rendering containment, reduced motion, and utility CSS maintainability.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not bundled scripts, browser automation, or a CSS testing engine.
Does not cover complete visual-system design or broad UX reviews.
Modern CSS features require browser compatibility checks for your supported environments.
The optional npx reference can execute an unpinned external package; review it before use.

use_cases.title: Repair Responsive Layouts
use_cases.description: Diagnose overflow, choose suitable layout engines, and adapt components to available space.

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared Component Styles
use_cases.description: Organize tokens, theme overrides, cascade layers, and reusable component sizing rules.

use_cases.title: Review CSS Rendering Costs
use_cases.description: Identify costly animation and containment patterns, then plan browser checks and reduced-motion alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Layout Engine
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HTML and CSS: [snippet]. Choose Flexbox or Grid for [layout goal], explain why, and suggest the smallest stylesheet change.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Component Overflow
prompt_templates.prompt: This component overflows at [width]. Review [HTML and CSS] for intrinsic minimum sizes, wrapping, and track sizing. Preserve intentional clipping.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Cascade Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [stylesheets] for specificity conflicts. Propose cascade layers and shared tokens that preserve [required appearance]. Avoid unnecessary important declarations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit CSS Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component styles] and [browser trace observations]. Recommend animation, containment, and reduced-motion changes. List compatibility checks and fallback options for [target browsers].

output_examples.input: A row of cards overflows on narrow screens even though the container width is limited.
output: Check whether long content forces each card to retain an intrinsic minimum width.
Allow flexible items to shrink and wrap content where needed.
Use a responsive grid when cards should occupy multiple rows.
Test narrow widths and long labels without hiding the overflow.

output_examples.input: Component padding changes unexpectedly after a utility stylesheet is added.
output: Compare the competing selectors and their cascade order.
Define an explicit layer order for base, component, and utility styles.
Keep selector specificity low and place shared spacing values in tokens.
Verify the intended padding across component states and themes.

output_examples.input: Animations feel slow, and a long page shifts while scrolling.
output: Inspect browser performance traces before assuming that animations are composited.
Prefer transform and opacity where they fit the intended motion.
Match rendering containment with realistic reserved sizes.
Verify reduced-motion behavior and accessibility before applying containment broadly.

best_practices: Provide relevant HTML, CSS, expected behavior, and supported browser versions.
Fix the underlying sizing or cascade issue before adding overrides or hiding overflow.
Validate responsive states, focus behavior, reduced motion, and performance in real browsers.
anti_patterns: Hide unintended overflow instead of investigating intrinsic sizes and wrapping.
Resolve every conflict with important declarations or deeply nested selectors.
Run the latest npx reference package without reviewing provenance and approving execution.

faq.question: What work does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It guides concrete CSS implementation and debugging for layout, responsive sizing, cascade, selectors, theming, and rendering performance.

faq.question: Does it provide a design system or UX review?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on stylesheet work and directs broader visual-system design and UX reviews to a separate skill.

faq.question: Can I use it with Tailwind?
faq.answer: Yes. Its guidance includes configured tokens, reusable component styles, and avoiding cascade conflicts in utility CSS.

faq.question: Are modern CSS features supported everywhere?
faq.answer: No. Check your target browsers and provide fallbacks for critical behavior, especially when using newer selectors or layout features.

faq.question: Does it automatically test or measure CSS?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains written guidance, not bundled testing tools. Browser inspection and performance traces require your available tooling.

faq.question: Do I need to run the reference command?
faq.answer: No. It is an optional reference. Prefer documentation links, or review and pin the package before approving any npx execution.
